import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_73/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_73/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation: JOIN on ["city", "city"]
# Both tables have 'city' column, join on this column
# df0 schema: ['city', 'date', 'fare', 'ride_id']
# df1 schema: ['right_index', 'city', 'driver_count', 'type']

# Perform inner join on 'city'
joined_df = pd.merge(df0, df1, on='city', how='inner')

# Select and reorder columns to match target schema:
# Target schema: ['type': string, 'city': string, 'fare': float, 'ride_id': float, 'driver_count': integer]

# Convert types accordingly:
# - 'type' is string (already string)
# - 'city' is string (already string)
# - 'fare' float (from df0)
# - 'ride_id' float (from df0) - convert to float
# - 'driver_count' integer (from df1) - convert to int

# Convert ride_id to float
joined_df['ride_id'] = joined_df['ride_id'].astype(float)

# Convert driver_count to int (if not already)
joined_df['driver_count'] = joined_df['driver_count'].astype(int)

# Select columns in target order
target_df = joined_df[['type', 'city', 'fare', 'ride_id', 'driver_count']]

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_73/target_multisource.csv"
target_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_73/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_73/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on 'city'
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Group by 'city' (the primary key)
# Aggregations:
# - type: take first (string)
# - fare: average (float)
# - ride_id: take first (float)
# - driver_count: take first (int)
result = joined.groupby("city", as_index=False).agg({
    "type": "first",
    "fare": "mean",
    "ride_id": "first",
    "driver_count": "first"
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
result = result[["type", "city", "fare", "ride_id", "driver_count"]]

# Write output
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_73/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
